subject: contract-paint-and-shell
text:
- **Paint and shell:** `paint_scene(PaintScene, &mut BaseDocument, scale, width, height, x_offset, y_offset)` (packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:43-51; examples/screenshot.rs:120-128; examples/paint_bench.rs:148-156; tests/blitz-tests/tests/background_size.rs:46); blitz-shell re-exports `BlitzApplication`, `BlitzShellEvent`, `BlitzShellProxy`, `View`, `WindowConfig`, `DataUriNetProvider` and winit's `ControlFlow`, `EventLoop`, `EventLoopProxy`, `Window` (packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:20-25; packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:44-45); `BlitzShellEvent` Poll, ResumeReady, RequestRedraw, CloseWindow, Accessibility, Embedder, Navigate, NavigationLoad, ResizeSettleCheck (packages/blitz-shell/src/event.rs:11-62), Embedder/Navigate/NavigationLoad left to embedders (packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:93-101); `BlitzShellProxy` pairs a winit proxy with an mpsc Sender and implements `NetWaker` (packages/blitz-shell/src/event.rs:70-103); `View::resume` dispatches ResumeReady and the embedder must call `complete_resume` (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:291-316; packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:318-362); `BlitzShellProvider` implements `ShellProvider` for redraw, cursor, title, IME, close, minimize, maximize, decorations, drag, clipboard, file dialog (packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:87-219); `DataUriNetProvider` serves only `data` (packages/blitz-shell/src/net.rs:49-69); shell bootstrap `BlitzShellProxy::new(event_loop.create_proxy())`, `BlitzApplication::new(proxy, receiver)`, `WindowConfig::new(Box::new(doc), renderer)`, `add_window`, `event_loop.run_app` (examples/inner_html.rs:25-33; examples/preact_script.rs:25-41);
 since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a password `input` (its `type` reading `password`) paints its value masked, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included: `draw_text_input_text` branches to the private `draw_masked_input_text`, which paints a bullet per character laid out by `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, so two values of one length paint byte-identical frames, focused or not; the caret is painted at the bullet of its index in the input's caret colour (private `caret_color`), and the field scrolls only to keep the caret in its content box, measured on the bullets rather than the editor's stored `scroll_offset`; a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — blitz-dom's pointer path lays them out through `layout_as_text_input`, scrolled as paint scrolls them, and moves the real editor to the character under the point (§Established Decisions → [Scrolling and input]), so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: one click at one offset into two values of one length lands on one index, and a double click selects the whole value (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:582-648; tests/blitz-tests/tests/password_caret_click.rs:83-121; packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:912-916; packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:966-973; packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:975-1049; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-headless-screenshot/report.md)

subject: contract-test-harness
contract-test-harness
text: - The harness's time (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18): the harness holds a `VirtualClock` its documents share — `HarnessOptions::into_config(self, &VirtualClock)` puts a clone in `DocumentConfig.clock`, so `from_html_with` and `from_vdom`, and through them `from_html` and `from_component`, build documents that read it, while `wrap(doc)` gives the harness a fresh `VirtualClock` and the wrapped document keeps the clock its own config gave it; `time()` reads that clock in seconds and `pump` resolves at it; `tick(dt)` advances it, a negative or non-finite `dt` moving nothing, and `advance_time(&mut self, by: Duration)` advances it by exactly `by`, each then pumping; `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never move it (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:48-76; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:125-133; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:152-174)

subject: contract-headless-stand
text:
- **Headless stand (seven_guis, native only):** `seven_guis::stand` — `LeanTask { Counter, FlightBooker, Timer, Crud }` with `ALL` and `task()`; pinned `VIEWPORT_WIDTH = 800`, `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT = 600`, `HIDPI_SCALE = 1.0`, `COLOR_SCHEME = ColorScheme::Light`; `font_ctx()` = `build_single_font_ctx(DEJAVU_SANS)`, system fonts off; `options(incremental) -> HarnessOptions` with the pinned viewport and bundled font, `net_provider: None` (offline through `DummyNetProvider`) and `base_url: None`, kept `None` for every caller (unit test `the_stand_options_stay_offline`), so every stand boot is offline but `boot_load`'s, which replaces that one field (below); `boot(LeanTask, HarnessOptions) -> Harness<DioxusDocument>` and `boot_timer(HarnessOptions) -> (Harness<DioxusDocument>, TimerTicks)`, each building a fresh `VirtualDom` whose root provides a `TimerTicks` context and renders `app::task_in_shell` with a no-op back handler; and `TIMER_TICK_MS: u32 = 100` with `timer_step(ticks: TimerTicks) -> impl FnMut(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>, u32)`, the Timer's time step for a driver session (`Session::with_time`, the Driver session contract below): handed the milliseconds asked, it delivers the whole ticks they hold through `TimerTicks::deliver`, carrying the remainder below one tick across calls (250 then 250 deliver 2 then 3 ticks), and returns nothing — the session, not the step, moves the harness's clock (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the ticks apply on the next pass (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:21-129; the time step as measured at escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock/report.md); it installs no telemetry, reads no env var and names no `blitz_net`, its load page's stand-in included.
 Supporting seven_guis API: `app::Task` (pub) and `app::task_in_shell(Task, EventHandler<()>) -> Element`, and `pub fn TaskShell`, the shell a test-local variant of a task mounts in so its unkeyed ids read as the task's (examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs:7; examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs:90; examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs:164); the crate-root `DEJAVU_SANS` woff2 bytes, one `include_bytes!` shared with the wasm entry (examples/seven_guis/src/lib.rs:7; examples/seven_guis/src/lib.rs:17); `tasks::timer::TimerTicks` (`deliver(n)`), which `Timer` reads with `try_use_context` — absent, the 100 ms `futures_timer::Delay` loop; present, one 0.1 s step capped at the duration per delivered tick (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:10-20; examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:47-55)

subject: contract-headless-stand
text: - `boot_cells(HarnessOptions) -> Harness<DioxusDocument>` mounts `Task::Cells` in `TaskShell` through the private `cells_root`, Cells staying no `LeanTask`: its screen passes the snapshot text's budget and reads in parts (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:131-139).

subject: contract-headless-stand
text: - `boot_load(HarnessOptions) -> Harness<DioxusDocument>` mounts a load page in `TaskShell` titled "Load" (the private `load_root` and `LoadPage`, its CSS `.load-root` · `.load-body` · `.load-btn` with `:hover` · `:active` · `.load-done`) holding two keyed elements — `load-fetch`, a Button "Load" in white on the stand accent `#3a5ce5` (hover `#2a4cd3`, active `#1f3fc1`), whose click links the page's one stylesheet, and `load-done`, a Paragraph "Loaded" at `display: none` until that sheet lands, no CSS selecting by id — its options' `net_provider` replaced by `Some(Arc::new(LoadNet))` through `..options`, every other field kept (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:141-152; examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:177-244).

subject: contract-headless-stand
text: - The private `LoadNet` implements `NetProvider`: each `fetch` answers the fixed `LOADED_CSS` (`.load-body .load-done { display: block; }`) for the fixed `LOAD_URL` `http://stand.test/load.css` from a thread of its own after `pub const LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY: Duration` (200 ms); it overrides no `is_noop`, so the harness counts its load, and holds no `blitz_net`, print, env read, socket or listener — a hand-written network stand-in beside the tests' `HeldNet` and `LateNet`, living in the stand module (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:154-175).

subject: contract-telemetry-bootstrap
text:
- **Telemetry bootstrap (escher-telemetry):** `init(ServiceIdentity) -> Result<InitOutcome, InitError>` installs the stderr sink and `init_with_writer(ServiceIdentity, W: MakeWriter)` a caller-given sink; `ServiceIdentity { name, version }` built by `service_identity!()` from the CALLER's `CARGO_PKG_NAME` / `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`; `InitOutcome::{Installed, AlreadyInstalled}` — a second call changes nothing; `InitError::ForeignSubscriber` (`Display` + `Error`, never a panic) when another subscriber or `log` logger is already global (packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:40-163). Line shape, one per printed event: `{RFC 3339 UTC time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name={name} service.version={version} {field}={value}…`, newlines escaped, string values Debug-quoted, a bridged `log` record printed under its `log.target` with that field omitted (packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:134-286).
 A second record class since 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans — a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (2026-10-09) as built — is one line per closed span whose target the allowlist admits, and no line when a span is created, recorded to, entered or exited: the same prefix, then `span={the span's name}` (`span` a reserved field name), the span's own fields in the order recorded, then the layer's close fields `message`, `time.busy` and `time.idle`, level and target the span's; every pair, `span` included, prints as the rule below judges an event's field of that name under the span's target — under an engine target `span`, `message` and both timings read `[redacted]` — a span of an outside target writes no byte at any point, the value of a field named in `CONTENT_FIELDS` is not stored at all, every other span field's value is held in process memory until the span closes and never written unless the rule prints it, and an event's line is unchanged, an event emitted inside a span included; the layer is stated once, in the private `sink_layer`, with `with_span_events(FmtSpan::CLOSE)` and the crate-private field formatter `SpanFields`, and no public item is added or changed (packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:102-116; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:138-177; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:200-250; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md).
 Target allowlist and scrub: the sink admits two public prefix sets, `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES` and `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES` (`escher_`, the underscore part of the prefix) — the fifth public scrub constant, beside `SAFE_FIELDS`, `CONTENT_FIELDS` and `REDACTED`; an event whose target starts with a prefix in `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES` prints only `SAFE_FIELDS`, every other field (`message` included) as `{name}=[redacted]`; an event whose target starts with a prefix in `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES` prints every field not in `CONTENT_FIELDS`, those redacted; an event whose target starts with a prefix of neither set is dropped whole — zero bytes, no time, target or newline — at every level, WARN and ERROR included, and whatever `RUST_LOG` names, a bridged `log` record judged by the target it was logged under (packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:22-111; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:144-148). Panic event: ERROR at target `escher_telemetry::panic`, fields `panic.file` · `panic.line` · `panic.column` · `panic.payload` (redacted), then the previous hook (packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs:4-24)
